note: Week 2026-09-14 build. Run fired on schedule Sunday 9/13 ~9:00pm CT; entries are recorded at official SIP regular-session closes of Friday 2026-09-11 and open Monday 9/14. PRIOR WEEK (9/8-9/11, a four-session Labor-Day week) closed -869.32 realized (-1.17%), 6 of 12 names green. Two names did all the damage: ORCL -7.53% (-452.88) and CPRT -8.13% (-424.00). ORCL actually BEAT and raised FY27 guidance on Thursday 9/10 and still fell 7% - the market is now willing to punish AI-capex buyers even on good numbers, and Larry Ellison cancelling his planned 50M-share sale did not stop it. CPRT's FQ4 print was the fourth consecutive disappointment. The energy leg worked as designed (VLO +1.98%, MGY +1.20%) but CVE was flat and the three-name sleeve netted about +167. Industrials were uniformly negative. THIS WEEK IS ORGANIZED AROUND THREE DATED EVENTS AND ONE HARD NUMBER. FIRST, THE FOMC MEETS WEDNESDAY 9/16. August CPI landed Friday 9/11 at +0.4% headline / +3.4% year-over-year, both in line, but core came in at +0.3% - a tenth hot - and futures now put roughly 85-90% odds on a 25bp HIKE to 4.00%, up from 66% a week ago. Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks repriced this whole cycle. The hike itself is priced; the dot plot and the press conference are not. The 10-year closed the week at 4.96% and the 30-year at 5.37%, and the VIX has broken above its 50-day toward 18. SECOND, GCC DIPLOMATS MEET THEIR IRANIAN COUNTERPART IN OMAN ON MONDAY 9/14 to discuss a temporary arrangement for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent spiked to $108.60 Thursday (+7.2%) on US-Iran strikes and then fell back below $105 Friday on the news of those talks. THIRD, FRIDAY 9/18 IS SEPTEMBER QUAD WITCHING. THE HARD NUMBER IS ORACLE'S CAPEX GUIDE. On Thursday night's call CFO Hilary Maxson guided FY capital expenditure to $90-95 BILLION. Oracle the stock fell 7% because it is the buyer; the sellers of that compute ripped on Friday - HPE +12.4%, DELL +12.0%, NTAP +8.5%, HPQ +8.4%, SMCI +7% - and HPE and DELL each did it on roughly 1.67x their 30-day average volume. That is the freshest, hardest, most volume-confirmed catalyst available this weekend, and it is a purchase-order number rather than a narrative. HOW THE BOOK IS BUILT. Technology (3) takes the Oracle capex trade three ways with deliberately different extension: HPE at $62.09 (1.66x volume, own raised FY26 guide 9/2, 3.4% below its high), DELL at $567.29 (1.67x volume, RBC initiation at $640, but AT its 52-week high after a 12% gap, so sized smallest in the book at 6.2%), and AVGO at $361.99 (no gap, 26.9% below its own high - the networking line of that budget is not yet in the price). Industrials (3) is the power-and-oil leg: VRT sits exactly on its 200-day after an 8.5% rates-driven washout on 9/9 with a $2.6B microgrid acquisition and a $369 average target, ETN is the only position carried forward that finished green, and UAL is the week's deliberate reversal - the book owned escalation through three energy names last week and the news flow has turned, so it owns the de-escalation instead, entered on 1.74x volume into Monday's Oman talks. Financials (3) is the explicit hedge against the book's own biggest risk: SCHW (largest position, every 25bp flows to net interest margin on several hundred billion of client cash, and it did NOT run into the event on Friday), MTB (Morgan Stanley top pick, $304 target, 12.7x earnings, carried forward because the catalyst it was bought for happens THIS week), and TRV at 10.0x reinvesting its float at 4.96%. GOOGL is the single Communication Services name and the cheapest mega-cap AI exposure anywhere at 17.0x. ILMN is the defensive healthcare sleeve on a fresh Friday upgrade with 1.38x volume. NEM is the smallest-conviction, clearest-job position: gold at $4,315 with $40T of federal debt is the only thing here that gains if Wednesday convinces the market the Fed is behind the curve. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT. ZERO ENERGY NAMES for the first time in weeks - Monday's Oman meeting makes every oil-levered position a coin flip on a diplomatic headline, and CTRA already fell 8.6% on Friday as the group unwound; UAL is the book's short-oil expression instead. ZERO DEFENSE - LHX printed a fresh 52-week low ($244.76) on Friday and bearish put sweeps hit LMT and NOC, so the complex is being de-rated on peace-talk odds rather than bid on war. CPRT was NOT re-bought despite a Friday Barrington upgrade to Outperform with a $40 target; adding to the week's biggest loser on one boutique call after a fourth straight weak print is not the discipline. IP was screened and rejected - BofA's Friday upgrade came with a price-target CUT to $46 from $48 and the stock closed below its open. META was screened and rejected in favour of GOOGL because it faded from its open on below-average volume. SMCI and ANET were rejected because both rose Friday on BELOW-average volume - no confirmation. THE BOOK'S MAIN UNCOVERED RISK is that the Oman talks collapse and Brent goes back through $110: that hurts UAL directly, lifts the CPI path, and there is no energy or defense position to offset it. That risk is carried in cash rather than in a hedge - 12 names, 87.9% deployed, 12.1% cash, the widest buffer this book has run.

positions.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/11 at $62.09, up 12.4% on 39.05M shares against a 23.53M 30-day average (1.66x), the single largest one-day move in the S&P 500 that session. The trigger was hard and dated: on Oracle's FQ1 call Thursday night, CFO Hilary Maxson guided full-year capital expenditure to $90-95 billion. That is a purchase-order number, not a narrative, and it lands on the vendors who build the racks, cooling and networking. HPE had already raised both its FY26 revenue and EPS guidance on 9/2 on record quarterly revenue, and management said publicly it cannot build AI servers fast enough to meet inbound demand. Oracle's capex figure confirms the constraint persists into FY27.
positions.risks: Up 12.4% in a single session and only 3.4% below the $64.25 52-week high set 6/2, so there is little cushion if the Wednesday dot plot is hawkish. Server hardware is a low-margin business where revenue growth does not automatically become earnings, and 32.4x trailing earnings already prices a lot of the AI mix shift. Oracle itself fell 7% on the same print, which is a reminder the market is willing to punish the AI-capex story even when the numbers are good.
positions.driver: The best volume-confirmed expression of the week's hardest new datapoint - Oracle's $90-95B capex guide - in a name that also carries its own raised guidance.

positions.name: Dell Technologies
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/11 at $567.29, up 12.0% on 14.47M shares versus an 8.68M 30-day average (1.67x), on the same Oracle capex guide. RBC Capital initiated coverage that morning with an Outperform rating and a $640 target, calling Dell a primary beneficiary of the global IT spending environment. Dell is the largest share gainer in AI server shipments and the ISG segment is where the Oracle dollars land directly.
positions.risks: This is the most extended entry in the book by a wide margin: the close of $567.29 is effectively the 52-week high of $567.75, set that same session, after a 12% gap. A one-week hold that buys an all-time high on a gap day is exposed to an immediate fill, and 32.9x earnings for a hardware business is a full multiple. Deliberately sized at the small end for exactly this reason - 6.2% of the book, so a 10% gap-fill costs roughly 60bp.
positions.driver: Same catalyst as HPE with equal volume confirmation and a fresh $640 initiation, sized down to respect the extension rather than skipped outright.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.catalyst: The third leg of the Oracle capex trade, and the only one entered with real room. Broadcom supplies the custom AI accelerators and the Tomahawk/Jericho switching silicon that sits inside every hyperscale AI cluster, so a $90-95B Oracle budget and the parallel sovereign-AI push Jensen Huang made at the G20 both route through it. Unlike HPE and DELL it did not gap on Friday - it closed at $361.99, 26.9% BELOW its $495.00 high of 6/3, meaning the networking line of the capex story is not in the price the way the server line now is.
positions.risks: 46.2x earnings on a $1.72 trillion market cap is the richest large-cap multiple in the book and the most sensitive to a hawkish dot plot, since semis carry the longest duration in the index. Volume on Friday was 21.2M against a 24.7M 30-day average - below average, so there was no confirming bid. Broadcom is also the most crowded AI position in institutional portfolios, which makes it a source of funds on any risk-off day.
positions.driver: Same theme as the two server names but bought 27% off its own high instead of at it - the capex dollars reach networking with a lag the tape has not yet paid for.

positions.name: Vertiv Holdings
positions.catalyst: Vertiv sells exactly the two line items Oracle just committed $90-95B to: rack power and liquid cooling. It closed Friday at $257.06, sitting directly on its 200-day moving average ($256.33) after an 8.5% drawdown on Wednesday 9/9 that was driven entirely by the 10-year yield hitting a three-year high, not by any company news. On 9/2 Vertiv agreed to acquire microgrid firm Utility Innovation for up to $2.6B ($1.45B cash at close plus $1.15B earnout), extending it upstream to the grid interconnect so data centers can secure power faster - the binding constraint on AI deployment. Sell-side average target is $369, 44% above the entry, and the next earnings report (est. 10/21) falls outside this window, so there is no binary event.
positions.risks: This is the most rate-sensitive name in the book and the FOMC decision is Wednesday. Wednesday 9/9 already demonstrated the mechanism - VRT fell 8.5% on a yield move with no news. Valuation is the weak point (57.9x, Benzinga Edge value score 1.46), and $250 is the level trend-followers defend; a break of the 200-day turns this from a bounce into a breakdown.
positions.driver: The purest picks-and-shovels claim on the Oracle capex dollar, bought on its 200-day after a rates-driven washout rather than after a gap.

positions.name: Eaton Corp.
positions.catalyst: Carried forward from last week's book, the only position retained, and the only industrial that finished green (+0.8%). It holds the UBS Buy upgrade with a $515 target - 21% above the entry - on a Q3 margin inflection from proactive pricing and better execution, and it is named in both of Nvidia's sovereign-AI framings as a power-infrastructure beneficiary alongside Vertiv. Closed Friday at $425.37, 11% below the $478.00 high of 8/12, with no scheduled event in the window.
positions.risks: 43.3x earnings for an electrical-equipment manufacturer is a growth multiple on a cyclical business. Volume Friday was 1.63M against a 1.73M 30-day average - no confirmation. It is also the second Industrials name levered to the same data-center power theme as VRT, so the two will correlate on any AI-capex de-rating; this is real concentration, not diversification.
positions.driver: The steady leg of the power theme - a large, profitable, order-backed compounder held for the margin inflection rather than for a headline.

positions.name: United Airlines Holdings
positions.catalyst: This is the book's deliberate reversal of last week's positioning. Brent traded as high as $108.60 on Thursday 9/10 (+7.2%) on US-Iran escalation, then fell back below $105 on Friday after Iranian state media reported plans for talks with Gulf states in Oman - and GCC diplomats are scheduled to meet their Iranian counterpart on MONDAY 9/14 to discuss a temporary arrangement for managing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. That meeting is inside this window. UAL closed Friday at $109.82 on 5.65M shares against a 3.24M 30-day average - 1.74x volume, the second-strongest confirmation in the book - having closed near the session high of $110.75 and well above its $108.79 open. Jet fuel is the single largest variable cost line for an airline, and at 10.3x earnings UAL is 20.9% below its $138.77 high of 6/30.
positions.risks: Explicitly binary on a diplomatic meeting, and diplomacy with Iran has failed repeatedly through 2026. If the Oman talks collapse, Brent goes back through $110 and UAL is the worst-positioned name in the book. Airlines are also the most cyclical consumer-facing business in the index, so a hawkish dot plot that raises recession odds hits it from the other side. This is the single largest idiosyncratic risk here and it is sized at 8.4%, not more.
positions.driver: The book owned the escalation last week through three energy names and it worked; the news flow has turned, so this week it owns the de-escalation instead - with 1.74x volume already confirming the rotation.

positions.name: Charles Schwab
positions.catalyst: The most direct equity beneficiary of the week's central event. Futures put roughly 85-90% odds on a 25bp hike to 4.00% at the Wednesday 9/16 FOMC after August core CPI printed +0.3% against a +0.2% consensus. Schwab earns the spread on several hundred billion dollars of client cash; every 25bp of policy rate flows into net interest margin with almost no offsetting cost, and the cash-sorting drag that suppressed the story through 2024-25 has largely run its course. At 19.5x earnings it is 6.4% below its $114.53 high of 8/24. Friday volume was 4.76M against a 7.31M 30-day average - it did NOT run into the event, which is the setup, not a flaw.
positions.risks: If Warsh hikes and then signals the cycle is finished, the curve rallies and the NII story is capped on the day it is delivered - a classic sell-the-news. Brokers also carry equity-market beta, so a sharp risk-off would hurt the trading and asset-management lines at the same time the rate line helps. And a 25bp hike at 85-90% odds is by definition mostly priced.
positions.driver: Largest position in the book, and the deliberate offset to it: the AI-infrastructure and airline legs all lose if the dot plot is hawkish, and this one wins.

positions.name: M&T Bank
positions.catalyst: Held from last week, where it finished green (+0.6%) in a week the book lost money. Morgan Stanley named it a top pick on 9/8 with a $304 target - 27% above the entry - on a net interest income beat-and-raise the firm argues the Street is underwriting, plus an underappreciated 2027 buyback. The thesis is unchanged and the catalyst is now four sessions closer: a 25bp hike lifts asset yields on a bank whose funding base has already repriced. 12.7x earnings and 1.36x book, 6.3% below its $255.95 high of 8/17.
positions.risks: Regional bank credit quality is the tail risk that cannot be underwritten from outside, and a hawkish dot plot that implies further hikes eventually becomes a credit problem rather than a margin benefit. Friday volume was 743K against a 948K 30-day average. If CPI revisions or a dovish surprise price the hike back out, the entire thesis inverts.
positions.driver: Cheapest asset-sensitive bank in the book with a live top-pick call, carried forward because the catalyst it was bought for happens this week rather than last.

positions.name: The Travelers Companies
positions.catalyst: The low-beta anchor, and a second way to be long higher rates. Travelers reinvests a large fixed-income float at market yields, and the 10-year note closed the week at 4.96% with the 30-year bond at 5.37% - both at or near multi-year highs. Rising book yields compound into net investment income quarter after quarter regardless of what equities do. At 10.0x earnings and 2.36x book it is the second-cheapest name in the book and 5.9% below its $398.70 high of 7/28, with no scheduled event in the window.
positions.risks: Hurricane season runs through November and a single large landfall event can erase a quarter of underwriting profit overnight - this is the one risk in the book that has nothing to do with the Fed or with oil. P&C pricing has also been decelerating as the hard market matures. As a defensive name it will lag badly if Wednesday produces a relief rally.
positions.driver: Third financial and the ballast: 10x earnings, a float being reinvested at 5%, and the lowest correlation to the AI-capex trade that makes up a third of the book.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.catalyst: The cheapest way to own the AI theme in the entire mega-cap complex, and the layer of the stack the book is otherwise not exposed to. Alphabet closed Friday at $338.50 on 24.7M shares against a 22.8M 30-day average (1.08x), finishing up from a $335.21 open and near the $342.97 session high - a quiet accumulation day rather than a gap. It trades at 17.0x earnings, the lowest multiple of any mega-cap AI name and roughly a third of Broadcom's, while being simultaneously a buyer of AI infrastructure (its own capex confirms the same cycle Oracle just guided to) and an owner of the models and applications that monetise it. 17.2% below its $408.61 high of 5/18.
positions.risks: No specific catalyst dated inside the window - this is a valuation-plus-momentum entry, not an event trade. Search-disruption and antitrust remedy risk remain live and are the reason the multiple is 17x rather than 25x. A $4.1T market cap means it moves with the index, so it offers little diversification against a broad hawkish selloff.
positions.driver: The one AI position in the book bought on valuation rather than on a catalyst - 17x earnings, closing up on above-average volume, 17% below its own high.

positions.name: Illumina
positions.catalyst: Upgraded on Friday 9/11 with a raised price target, one of a short list of names to get a genuine upgrade that day, and it traded 2.41M shares against a 1.75M 30-day average - 1.38x confirming volume - with the session high of $208.36 printed intraday. The sequencing recovery is real: the stock has run from an $88.00 low on 10/14/25 to $206.45 and sits 10.9% below its $231.81 high of 8/27. Healthcare also functions as the book's defensive sleeve into Wednesday, being the sector least mechanically sensitive to the policy rate.
positions.risks: 38.5x earnings for a business whose instrument placements are still dependent on academic and pharma budgets that are themselves under funding pressure. No event in the window. The stock has more than doubled off its low in eleven months, so a large amount of the recovery is already banked, and life-science tools sold off hard earlier in September on the Novartis Phase 3 failures that de-rated the whole sector.
positions.driver: Fresh Friday upgrade with 1.38x volume confirmation in the one sector whose earnings are least affected by a 25bp hike.

positions.name: Newmont Corporation
positions.catalyst: The hedge against the outcome that would damage every other position here: the Fed hiking and inflation still not coming down. Gold closed the week at $4,315 an ounce after a 1.93% profit-taking day Thursday, with silver at $63.45. The bid is fiscal rather than monetary - $40 trillion of US federal debt with a 30-year bond at 5.37% and no credible consolidation path - which is why bullion has advanced all year against RISING real rates rather than falling ones. Newmont closed at $126.81, only 6.3% below its $135.29 high of 8/25, at 16.0x earnings, and as the largest listed gold producer it carries direct operating leverage to the metal.
positions.risks: Mechanically, a hawkish dot plot raises real rates and that is textbook bad for a non-yielding asset - the fiscal bid has overridden that relationship all year but there is no guarantee it does so on Wednesday. Friday volume was 5.55M against a 7.93M 30-day average, so there was no confirming bid, and gold had just been sold on Thursday. Miners also add operational risk (grades, costs, jurisdictions) on top of the metal.
positions.driver: Smallest conviction, clearest job: the only position in the book that gains if Wednesday convinces the market the Fed is behind the curve.
